recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which rule you use for three factors and what the three terms look like.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the three-factor product rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the rule for three factors before touching this question. Each term differentiates exactly one factor and leaves the other two unchanged, so there are three terms and no more.
steps.memory_tip: Three factors give three terms, and in each term only one factor carries a prime.
lines: For three functions u, v, w the product rule reads
Take u = x,  v = eˣ,  w = sin x
Then u′ = 1,  v′ = eˣ,  w′ = cos x

recall.must_convey: That the three-factor product rule d/dx(uvw) = u′vw + uv′w + uvw′ is used with u = x, v = eˣ, w = sin x.
accept: use the product rule for three functions u v w
u dash v w plus u v dash w plus u v w dash
take u as x, v as e power x and w as sin x
moodu functions unnappudu moodu terms vasthayi
three factors so three terms, one prime in each

steps.why: The rule stated in full is worth a mark on its own, and naming u, v, w with their derivatives first prevents a factor being differentiated twice in the same term.
common_mistakes: Using the two-factor rule and producing only two terms.
Differentiating two factors in the same term, for example writing 1 · eˣ · cos x.

steps.label: Substitute the three derivatives and take eˣ out
steps.margin_note: Second mark. eˣ appears in all three terms, so it comes out as a common factor. Inside the bracket, sin x appears twice and groups as (1 + x) sin x.
steps.memory_tip: eˣ is its own derivative, so it appears in all three terms and can be taken out of the whole answer.
lines: d/dx(xeˣ sin x) = (1)eˣ sin x + x(eˣ) sin x + xeˣ(cos x)
= eˣ sin x + xeˣ sin x + xeˣ cos x
Take eˣ common from all three terms:
= eˣ[sin x + x sin x + x cos x]

lines.text: ∴ d/dx(xeˣ sin x) = eˣ[(1 + x) sin x + x cos x]

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives eˣ sin x + xeˣ sin x + xeˣ cos x, which factors as eˣ[(1 + x) sin x + x cos x].
accept: e power x sin x plus x e power x sin x plus x e power x cos x
take e power x common from all three terms
the answer is e power x into bracket one plus x sin x plus x cos x
e power x ni common teesukunte answer vasthundi
group the two sin x terms as one plus x sin x

steps.why: Factoring eˣ out is what turns three long terms into the short printed form, and it also makes a sign slip visible because every term inside the bracket is positive.
common_mistakes: Writing d/dx(eˣ) as xeˣ⁻¹, treating eˣ as a power of x.
Leaving the answer as three unfactored terms and losing the tidy form the key expects.

insider_note: THREE functions multiplied, so the product rule has three terms, each differentiating one factor. Taking eˣ out at the end is what makes the answer compact.
